title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 92
paragraphs: So the Aeginetans treated one another. When the Athenians arrived, they fought against them with seventy ships, were beaten at sea, and called on the same allies as before — the Argives — for help. The Argives, however, would no longer come, having a grievance because ships from Aegina, pressed into service by Cleomenes, had put in to the Argolid and the crews had landed alongside the Lacedaemonians; men from Sicyonian ships had landed with them too in that same invasion. As punishment, the Argives had fined both states, a thousand talents in all: five hundred each. The Sicyonians acknowledged that they had done wrong and agreed to pay a hundred talents to settle their debt. The Aeginetans, however, refused to admit any wrongdoing and dug in their heels. For this reason, when Aegina now asked for help, no Argive came at the state's expense; but volunteers came, about a thousand of them, led by a commander named Eurybates, who had trained as a pentathlete. Most of these men never returned home — they were killed by the Athenians on Aegina. Eurybates himself, fighting in single combat, killed three opponents in succession and was himself killed by the fourth, Sophanes of Deceleia.
